fields.quoted_span: It prohibits terminations of tenancies without just cause and requires relocation assistance for no-fault evictions.
fields.note: D040 supports the at-fault and no-fault cause lists, annual registration, the Right to Counsel and Renters' Protections notices, the Fair Market Rent nonpayment rule, the 3-business-day filing and the point that the JCO does not regulate rent increases. It does not mention the Declaration of Intent to Evict, the Chart A relocation parity, the 15-day payment or escrow timing, the one-month single-family rule or the rent offset. Those come only from the D043 bulletins.

fields.quoted_span: All eviction notices issued to tenants in the City of Los Angeles must be filed with LAHD within three (3) business days of service on the tenant.
fields.note: The 3-business-day filing and the six-month or lease-expiry coverage trigger are in D040. The Chart A dollar amounts, the single-family one-month rent rule and the 15-day payment are not in D040.
The field is empty. D040 gives no effective date for the JCO itself. The dates in the effective_date_note belong to sub-rules and are not an effective date for the JCO.

fields.quoted_span: It prohibits terminations of tenancies without just cause and requires relocation assistance for no-fault evictions.
fields.note: The page describes the JCO in the present tense as operative law, which is consistent with in_force.

fields.quoted_span: The JCO covers most residential properties in the City of Los Angeles that are not regulated by the City’s Rent Stabilization Ordinance (RSO).
fields.note: The RSO exclusion, buildings newer than October 1, 1978, single-family dwellings, the six-month or lease-expiry condition and the list of other exceptions all appear in D040.
D040 names the Just Cause For Eviction Ordinance (JCO) but never cites L.A. Mun. Code § 165.03 or any other code section.
